newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Top senators say enlargement will be ratified.
newsitem.headline: Top senators say enlargement will be ratified.

text.p: A group of top U.S. senators said on Wednesday they believed the U.S. Congress would ratify NATO's planned eastward expansion, but warned that opposition to the enlargement process was growing.

Senator Trent Lott of Mississippi, the Senate Majority leader, said the prospects for ratification were good, but that hard questions would be asked over the cost of expanding NATO to include former communist foes from eastern Europe.

"There are many issues the Senate will examine in the ratification process -- overall costs, how cost will be shared by future and current NATO members, the relationship with Russia, reassurance to those not invited," he said.

Lott, who is heading a high-level bipartisan Senate delegation to Europe ahead of next week's NATO summit in Madrid, was addressing a press conference after a day of talks at the alliance's headquarters.

Lott said his team supported the decision of U.S. President Bill Clinton to invite Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic at the summit to join the West's defence organisation, but stressed the "door would remain open" for other new members at a later date.
Clinton, determined to keep costs in check and ensure ratification by a Republican-led Congress, has rejected allied pressure to broaden the enlargement to include Slovenia and Romania
